body:
P2-12 PLAN 3/6: IDENTITY, the N-14 fix (facts read in the code, 14 Nov 2026; replaces the first version of this note)
The phone has FOUR rules for "which catalogue artist is this artist": (a) libraryArtistCatalogueProvider (catalogue_providers.dart:156): same folded name and albumCount > 0, then the releases of the three best known against the library's album titles, else most fans; (b) AlertsService (alerts_service.dart:320): the FIRST same-name artist, kept on the phone (alerts.catalogueArtistIds), so it can disagree with the page; (c) catalogueSearchProvider (request_providers.dart:243): most fans; (d) openArtistByName (open_artist.dart:45): exact name, then fans.
The server has the pieces: artist_finder.pick_artist_picture proves an artist from ONE of its own songs (ADR-R46) and returns ArtistPicture.source_id, the catalogue's artist id, which deezer_artist_picture throws away. The phone's artist row id is the music server's artist id (getArtists, sync_engine.dart:509) and artist_picture is keyed by the same id: the key both sides have. A name key would need P2-25's normaliser (B-37).
DECISION: extend N-15's table; no second table, no second rule (docs/30 question 4). Migration 0014 rebuilds artist_picture as artist_catalogue (create, copy, drop, rename): same key and name, picture columns kept (outcome nullable: NULL = a visit learned the identity, nobody looked for a picture), new columns catalogue_id (NULL = the catalogue has no such artist), basis, decided_at, recheck_at, evidence (JSON: candidates, the matching song or albums). One function identify_artist() beside pick_artist_picture (reused) is called by the artist finder (a picture found by song evidence records the identity at no extra request) and by the route.
THE RULE (one, ordered by cost): (1) one request, the artists named like it: exactly one same folded name with albumCount > 0 -> 'only'. (2) several -> song evidence: the track search for up to 3 of the artist's own songs; a hit counts when its title is the song's and its artist is the library artist or leads the credit -> 'song'. (3) none proves it -> releases of the 3 best known against the library's album titles for the artist -> 'overlap' (at least one shared title). (4) else most fans -> 'fans'. No same-name artist: song evidence for up to 2 songs, else a miss (catalogue_id NULL, recheck in 7 days). An outage writes nothing (B-124). Rechecks: 'fans' after 30 days or when the library's albums for the artist change; 'only', 'overlap', 'song' after 180 days; 'host' never (reserved). Two catalogue artists of one name: the library artist links to ONE, the other stays an unowned row in search. 'fans' can pick the wrong namesake: shortest-lived basis, recorded.
TRUST (advisor): the route stores a household-wide fact keyed by libraryArtistId, so a phone's input must not decide it (the class of B-86: a bad phone could give everybody's page X the discography of a name Y). The server takes the name for that id from the music server itself (the cached getArtists the finder already reads); the phone's name is only a search hint when the music server cannot answer; a row whose id and name disagree is never stored; an id the music server does not know is a 404 that writes nothing. Test: a mismatched id and name writes nothing (docs/30 F: the wrong party gets nothing).
STOP-GAPS (trigger + a grepped comment STOP-GAP(P2-12 slice N)): the phone keeps name-based ownership marking (LibraryMatcher.findArtist) for rows with no libraryArtistId (B-46 stays partly open) until slice 8 has identified every library artist; alerts_service.dart keeps its own map until slice 6. NEVER a phone-side column (the N-14 note's interim): a fifth place to repair.
RISK: the key assumes the phone's artist ids stay the music server's. P2-20 moves the phone's copy off getArtists onto the Encore feeds: they must carry that id, or P2-20 names the fallback. An id that changes when a Host fixes a tag is harmless: the artist is identified again.
